correctness.rationale: The diagonal equation follows from e_i^2 images. A nonzero determinant term forces every scaling scalar onto an odd-order squaring cycle. Equal color multiplicities characterize invertible compatible block matrices, yielding the exact expectation. Minimal-support symmetry forces one isolated weighted directed r-cycle. Distinct overlapping cycles are impossible and disjoint event intersections are negligible. Bounding fixed compatible matrix subspaces by (n-s)^2+s^2/r gives the uniform larger-support tail. Exact GL_n asymptotics yield the displayed constant and the conditional group size h. The attached checker directly enumerates all GL matrices in six finite configurations and confirms both mean and event counts, plus an F8 witness; finite tests do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: The probability a random perfect evolution algebra exhibits diagonal symmetry is a natural invariant of the labelled finite-field ensemble. Beyond known graph-based constraints, the theorem gives the first permitted dimension, exact expected stabilizer order for every n, a sharp q-dependent rare-event decay with explicit constant and a conditional cyclic order. These quantify previously unmeasured family-wide symmetry behavior and distinguish fields with and without odd-order units; the result is not a mere renaming or isolated finite table.
